hypothesis: V3 Candidate Hypothesis 3: Month-End Flow Bias
research_question: Does FX price behaviour during the final trading day / final trading hours of each month show a repeatable directional OR volatility bias materially different from ordinary trading days?

pre_registered_protocol.window_a_final_trading_day: last UTC calendar date per (year, month) with H1 data present
pre_registered_protocol.window_b_final_trading_hours: last 4 H1 bars of that day (fixed, not tuned)
pre_registered_protocol.control: every other trading day in DEVELOPMENT (Window A); each ordinary day's own last-4-bars (Window B)
pre_registered_protocol.volatility_measure: realized vol = sqrt(sum of squared H1 log returns) within the window
pre_registered_protocol.survival_bar: p<0.05 mean/median return AND hit rate significantly != 50%, consistent sign across ~4/4 years, for at least one measure, AND survives realistic Bid/Ask costs
pre_registered_protocol.automatic_rejection: sign flips across years; hit rate indistinguishable from 50%; raw pooled effect not significant; realistic costs erase/reverse a nominally significant raw edge; no material stable volatility difference either
pre_registered_protocol.pre_acknowledged_limitation: ~12 month-ends/year x 3.9yr development window gives ~47 events/instrument (~94 combined) - below the project's 150-event minimum-sample convention before any stratification. Flagged as the leading risk when this hypothesis was originally proposed and ranked weakest of the three V3 candidates for this reason.

returns.interpretation: No hit rate anywhere is significantly different from 50%. Primary pooled close-to-close/intraday tests are not significant (p~0.21-0.22). Only the last-4h window shows a nominally significant difference from control, driven almost entirely by EUR_USD - GBP_USD shows essentially nothing anywhere.

volatility.interpretation: Realized volatility in the final 4 hours of the month is ~23% higher than ordinary days, nominally significant (p=0.012) - consistent with well-documented real month-end/fix-related activity. This is a volatility fact, not a directional edge, and per the pre-registered protocol is necessary but not sufficient to validate this hypothesis as a directional trading idea; it would point toward a differently-shaped idea (volatility timing) if pursued.

effect_size.interpretation: Small effect sizes throughout, below what is normally considered even a small reliable effect.

stability_by_year_combined_close_to_clos.interpretation: Direction is negative in 4/5 years but flips positive in 2022; only 2/5 years individually reach nominal significance - with ~15-20 tests run across the full analysis, this is close to what chance alone predicts.

cost_adjusted_edge.direction_used: pooled combined-sample observed mean sign (negative/short), chosen once from the full sample, not cherry-picked per instrument/year
cost_adjusted_edge.interpretation: Not statistically significant even using hindsight to pick the direction; GBP_USD alone would have lost money shorting.

verdict: REJECTED. The directional hypothesis fails its own pre-committed survival bar on every count: no significant pooled directional return (close-to-close or intraday), no hit rate distinguishable from 50% anywhere, sign inconsistent across years (2022 flips positive), and the cost-adjusted edge is not significant even using the generous pooled-sample direction chosen with hindsight. The one genuine finding - ~23% higher realized volatility in the final 4 hours of the month, nominally significant - is a volatility fact consistent with known month-end/fix activity, not evidence of the directional flow bias this hypothesis specifically asked about, and does not by itself clear the bar to justify a V3 build. Combined with the pre-acknowledged small sample (96, below the 150-event convention), there is no defensible edge here.
does_not_proceed_to: V3 build - hypothesis rejected at the cheap-falsification stage, before any strategy/entry-exit code was written. All three original V3 candidates (Cross-Instrument Lead-Lag, Weekend Gap Fade, Month-End Flow Bias) are now rejected.
note_for_future_work: The elevated last-4h volatility finding, while not sufficient to validate this hypothesis, could seed a genuinely different future hypothesis (volatility-timing / elevated-activity-window exploitation) if pursued later - explicitly not acted on here, per the project's standing discipline against building on a pattern discovered mid-analysis without independent, advance justification.
